description: Agent-based, networked social adoption model of mask-wearing behavior with market supply, policy, enforcement, and information dynamics. Persons interact over a small-world social network; beliefs and adoption evolve via peer influence, information campaigns, and enforcement; purchases occur under inventory, price, and rationing constraints; locations apply policies that affect compliance.

parameters.location_routine_profile: draw by location_mix and age/employment heuristics

parameters.message_content: Mask-wearing reduces transmission; use properly in public places.
parameters.policy_schedule: mandate masks in public locations from day 45 onward

modules.name: SocialInfluenceModule
modules.description: Updates individual beliefs (risk perception, perceived benefit/cost) from peers via social contagion and intrinsic susceptibility.

update_rule.pseudocode:
for each person i:
  neighbors = i.network_neighbors
  peer_adoption = mean(adoption_state[n] for n in neighbors)
  household_push = Household[i.household_id].household_norm_strength * mean(adoption_state[h] for h in Household[i.household_id].member_ids)
  social_signal = peer_attention_weight * peer_adoption + (1 - peer_attention_weight) * household_push
  delta_risk = social_influence_strength * i.social_influence_susceptibility * (social_signal - i.risk_perception)
  i.risk_perception = clamp(i.risk_perception + risk_perception_update_rate * delta_risk, 0, 1)
  i.perceived_benefit = clamp(i.risk_perception * (0.5 + 0.5 * i.trust_in_authorities), 0, 1)
  i.perceived_cost = clamp(1 - i.trust_in_authorities * baseline_trust_mean, 0, 1)
notes: Beliefs drift toward neighbors' observed adoption as a proxy for social proof.
Household norms amplify within-household convergence.
Perceived cost inversely related to trust; perceived benefit rises with risk perception and trust.

modules.name: InformationCampaignModule
modules.description: Applies authority and media information effects to individuals' risk perception and trust.

update_rule.pseudocode:
for each person i:
  exposure = communication_intensity * info_campaign_effectiveness
  media_effect = sum_over_media( media.reach * media.credibility * (1 - media_bias_std * abs(media.bias)) )
  risk_boost = disease_prevalence_signal_amplitude * exposure * (0.5 + 0.5 * media_effect)
  trust_adjust = 0.1 * exposure * (media_effect - 0.5)
  i.risk_perception = clamp(i.risk_perception + risk_boost * (1 - i.risk_perception), 0, 1)
  i.trust_in_authorities = clamp(i.trust_in_authorities + trust_adjust, 0, 1)
notes: Information raises risk perception in proportion to campaign intensity and media credibility.
Media bias reduces effective credibility; can slightly shift trust.

modules.name: RetailMarketModule
modules.description: Manages retailer inventory, pricing, rationing, restocking, supply shocks, and sales to individuals.

notes: Demand function is provided by persons (AdoptionDecisionModule hook).
Simple inventory-aware pricing: raises price on low inventory, decays slightly otherwise.
Affordability constraint uses affordability_sensitivity fraction of income per visit.

modules.name: AdoptionDecisionModule
modules.description: Determines adoption state, mask type selection, adherence updates, and replacement/discard behavior based on beliefs, costs, and policy context.

update_rule.pseudocode:
for each person i:
  # utility for adopting vs not
  expected_effectiveness = max_over_types( mask_effectiveness_by_type[t] - affordability_sensitivity * normalized_price[t] )
  policy_bonus = mandate_compliance_bias if any_mandate_in_daily_routine(i) else 0
  U_adopt = perceived_benefit_weight * i.perceived_benefit * (expected_effectiveness + policy_bonus) - i.perceived_cost
  U_not = 0
  i.adoption_state = 1 if U_adopt > U_not and i.masks_on_hand > 0 else 0
  # choose mask type if adopting and purchasing today
  if i.adoption_state == 1 and i.masks_on_hand == 0:
    choose t* = argmax_t( mask_effectiveness_by_type[t] - affordability_sensitivity * normalized_price[t] )
    request purchase of qty based on replacement_interval_days_by_type[t*]
    i.mask_type_owned = t*
  # adherence decay and replacement
  i.adherence_level = clamp(i.adherence_level * (1 - adherence_decay_rate) + 0.1 * i.adoption_state, 0, 1)
  if i.adoption_state == 1 and day % replacement_interval_days_by_type[i.mask_type_owned] == 0 and i.masks_on_hand > 0:
    i.masks_on_hand -= 1
notes: Utility balances effectiveness and affordability.
Mandate presence increases utility to adopt via policy_bonus.
Adherence decays without reinforcement and increases when adopting.
Replacement consumes stock at type-specific intervals.

modules.name: PolicyEnforcementModule
modules.description: Allocates enforcement, applies warnings/fines, and updates compliance based on mandates and enforcement probabilities.

notes: Enforcement capacity limits daily actions.
Warnings and fines increase perceived cost of non-adoption, nudging compliance.

modules.name: MobilityAndContextModule
modules.description: Assigns daily person-time across location types based on routines and capacity; determines mandate exposure and possible entry denial.

notes: Simple daily time allocation; denials occur in required contexts when unmasked.

modules.name: AuthorityPolicyModule
modules.description: Sets and updates mask policy states at locations according to schedule.

notes: Can be extended to staged or rolling mandates by location type.

modules.name: AdoptionAggregator
modules.description: Aggregates observables (adoption, compliance, purchases, inequality, stockouts) and computes derived metrics.

update_rule.pseudocode:
adoption_rate = mean(Person.adoption_state)
for each context policy in {required, recommended, optional}:
  compliance[policy] = sum_i( Person.adoption_state_i * time_in_policy_context_i(policy) ) / sum_i( time_in_policy_context_i(policy) )
purchase_coverage = mean( Person.masks_on_hand >= expected_needs_i ) where expected_needs_i derived from adherence and policy exposure
inequality = gini( group_means_by_income_quintile(Person.adoption_state) )
warnings = count(enforcement_actions_daily.type == 'warning')
fines = count(enforcement_actions_daily.type == 'fine')
for each type t: stockout_frequency[t] = moving_fraction_over_window( Retailer.stockout_flags_by_type[:,t], window=7 )
avg_price_by_type[t] = mean(Retailer.price_by_type[t])
# elasticity: regress adoption_rate on avg price index over last elasticity_estimation_window days
price_index = mean_t( avg_price_by_type[t] )
if day >= elasticity_estimation_window:
  elasticity = OLS(log(adoption_rate_{t}) ~ log(price_index_{t})) slope over window
else: elasticity = NaN
notes: Compliance is time-weighted by context exposure.
Purchase coverage compares stock to expected needs from adherence and replacement schedules.
Gini computed over income-group mean adoptions.
Elasticity estimated via short-window log-log regression.

algorithms.peer_influence_update: Linear pooling of peer and household signals with bounded updates
algorithms.information_campaign_effect: Exposure-scaled perturbation to risk and trust with media credibility weighting
algorithms.utility_based_adoption: Discrete choice between adopt vs not using perceived benefit, cost, effectiveness, and price
algorithms.budget_constrained_purchasing: Greedy purchase subject to retailer inventory and per-visit limits
algorithms.price_adjustment: Inventory-ratio-driven dynamic pricing with markup when near stockout
algorithms.enforcement_allocation: Priority sampling of noncompliers under capacity; stochastic outcome warning/fine
algorithms.mobility_assignment: Dirichlet draw of daily time shares adjusted by location_mix and entry denials
algorithms.inequality_gini: Gini coefficient over group means (income quintiles)
algorithms.elasticity_estimation: Rolling-window OLS on log adoption vs log average price index
